newsitem.title: USA: Enzo files patent for immunosuppressant.
newsitem.headline: Enzo files patent for immunosuppressant.

text.p: Enzo Biochem Inc said Thursday it has filed a U.S. patent application for a compound and "novel procedure" that could allow for the management of undesirable immunologic complications of HIV, hepatitis and other infectious diseases by selectively suppressing the immune response to such diseases.

The procedure and product can be used with a new generation of gene-based medicines or traditional biochemical medicines, said the company, that would otherwise elicit an undesirable immune response during the course of treatment.
The patent application describes processes designed to create a tolerance to specific antigens and other forms of immune stimulus, while maintaining overall immune competence in the subject.
The company added that these processes could be used proactively, such as in preparation for organ transplantation or gene therapy, or reactively, in the case of acute infections or chronic diseases.
Enzo is engaged in the research, development and manufacture of health care products based on molecular biology and genetic engineering techniques.
